I am Dr. Agent, and I see you are an infant presenting with recurrent stridor and wheezing; since infants cannot speak, please have your caregiver describe exactly what triggers these symptoms, such as crying, feeding, or lying down. Additionally, could you clarify if there are any choking episodes or foreign body ingestions associated with these events?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
REQUEST IMAGES: Upper_Airway_Swallowing_Study

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray Findings: Evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch; Barium Swallow Findings: Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring; Echocardiogram Findings: Confirmatory findings of a double aortic arch.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch with Vascular Ring. Based on the confirmatory imaging and echo results showing tracheal and esophageal compression, this congenital anomaly explains the recurrent stridor and wheezing. I will now consult Cardiothoracic Surgery to discuss potential surgical correction to prevent airway obstruction.
